news.title: 2026 WAFF Amputee World Cup: Mubarik's double sends Ghana into semi-final
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark YEN.com.gh as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Ghana's Black Challenge have reached the semi-finals of the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup for the first time in the nation's history, following a 2-0 quarter-final victory over Egypt on Thursday, November 19. Striker Mohammed Mubarik delivered a man-of-the-match performance at the tournament in Mexico, netting both goals to guide Stephen Richard Obeng's side past their North African opponents and into the last four of the global competition. The forward's brace extended his tally to six goals for the tournament.

news.title: 2026 Amputee World Cup: Ghana beat Egypt 2-0 to reach semifinals
news.lede: Ghana's national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have advanced to the semifinals of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico after defeating Egypt 2-0 in the quarterfinals on Thursday. A second-half brace from Mohammed Mubarik secured the victory for the two-time African champions, who are now just one win away from reaching the World Cup final. The victory marks a significant milestone for the Black Challenge, who have now surpassed their previously documented best World Cup finishes of sixth place, achieved in 2010 and 2012. Ghana will face either Türkiye or Japan in the semifinals as they continue their pursuit of a historic World Cup title.

news.title: 'Really proud': Aussie U17s' stunning World Cup win over powerhouse ... as teen prodigy dazzles
news.lede: Australia's Under 17 team has pulled off a staggering upset over football powerhouse Argentina to begin their U17 World Cup campaign in spectacular fashion. Having failed to qualify for the last two tournaments, the Joeys made their return to the biggest stage for the first time since 2019 with a 2-0 win in Qatar, with rising prodigy Akol Akon front and centre. The 17-year-old was initially not expected to be at the World Cup, with A-League club Sydney FC refusing to release him for the tournament, citing a need for him to play for them. But having secured a workaround, Akon, who next season will head to Major League Soccer side Colorado Rapids, dazzled to lead the Joeys to a famous win.

news.title: MTN rewards Flamingos with N150m after World Cup success
news.lede: MTN Nigeria has reaffirmed its commitment to Nigerian football and youth development with a N150 million reward and a one-year data package for the Flamingos following the team’s historic success at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. The company announced the reward package at a reception hosted in honour of head coach Akeem Busari’s squad at its corporate headquarters in Lagos. Read Also: Sanwo-Olu rewards Flamingos with N10m each, iPhones after World Cup victory. Speaking at the reception, Karl Toriola, chief executive officer of MTN Nigeria, congratulated the team on their achievement and praised the resilience that defined their journey to the title.

news.title: Fifa sparks tension with demand for tax-free status in UK for Women’s World Cup
news.lede: It also wants exchange-rate fees exemption for 2035. Fifa at loggerheads with UK’s four FAs and government. Fifa is at loggerheads with the UK’s government and four football associations over the world governing body’s demands for tax-free status and exemptions from exchange-rate fees at the 2035 Women’s World Cup. The UK bid to host the tournament is due to be ratified at an extraordinary Fifa congress in Zurich on Monday and the Guardian has learned there is tension behind the scenes over many of Fifa’s requirements, which multiple sources involved in the discussions have indicated will not be met.

news.title: Meet Morocco's other lions: the players competing for the amputee football World Cup
news.lede: Morocco’s amputee football team plays Angola, the 2018 world champions, tonight for a place in the World Cup semifinals, four straight wins into its run in Mexico and four years removed from a debut tournament in which one of its players asked supporters for something other than sympathy. Mohcine Chrharh, now the team’s captain, had just scored twice in a 4-0 win over Argentina at that 2022 World Cup, less than a year after the national team was formed, when he told El Botola: “Moroccans may sympathize with us because we are amputees, but we would rather have their encouragement and support than their sympathy.” His teammates include a goalkeeper who once coached a neighborhood futsal team, footballers who left Moroccan clubs to establish careers in Poland and Turkey, and younger players who emerged from amputee football associations in Agadir.
